occupations.cat: Labourers in mining, construction, manufacturing and transport

n.story:
In the coming years, your role will remain grounded in the physical world, but the tools you use will become significantly smarter. While robots still struggle with the dexterity required for deep cleaning in cluttered, dynamic factory environments, AI will take over the repetitive 'supply' tasks. Automated systems will increasingly handle the replenishment of machines, freeing you from the most monotonous parts of the workflow. Your role will evolve toward a 'technical custodian,' where you oversee the cleanliness and readiness of high-tech equipment that requires a human touch to maintain.

AI will amplify your effectiveness through Augmented Reality (AR) and smart sensors. Instead of guessing which cleaning agent is best for a specific industrial residue, AI-powered tools will provide instant chemical recommendations and safety protocols. You will become more of a troubleshooter; while the AI monitors inventory and basic floor scrubbing, you will handle the complex, non-standardized physical tasks that require human adaptability. Your value will be defined by your ability to work alongside automated systems, ensuring the physical environment remains optimal for both human and robotic workers.
auto: Repetitive machine feeding and tool replenishment
Basic floor scrubbing in large, open areas
Routine safety gear compliance checks via cameras
amp: Precision selection of cleaning chemicals via AI databases
AR-guided maintenance and tool usage diagnostics
Enhanced situational awareness of factory floor hazards
Optimized scheduling of cleaning tasks based on machine usage
Improved safety through real-time PPE monitoring
n.adv: Embrace digital interfaces and AR tools as they are introduced to the factory floor; being the person who knows how to interface with the 'smart' factory systems will make you indispensable.

n.story:
Your role is evolving from a manual laborer to a high-tech maritime preservationist. While the core of your craft—the tactile application of oakum and cotton—remains a human-only skill, the 'guesswork' of the shipyard is disappearing. AI now handles the complex mathematics of material estimation and waste reduction, ensuring you arrive at the hull with exactly what you need, while computer vision instantly identifies wood species and structural anomalies that the naked eye might miss.

As sensors become embedded in modern and restored hulls, your responsibility shifts toward proactive maintenance. You will use AI-driven diagnostic tools to monitor hull integrity in real-time, allowing you to address leaks before they become emergencies. You are no longer just a sealer of seams; you are a data-informed guardian of vessel longevity, using augmented reality to overlay regulatory requirements and safety protocols directly onto your field of vision as you work.
auto: Calculating material quantities and waste ratios
amp: Early-stage leak detection via acoustic sensors
Precision material optimization for complex hull geometries
Real-time safety monitoring and risk prediction
Digital logging of historical restoration techniques
tools: Computer vision for wood and defect identification
Acoustic sensor arrays for hull monitoring
n.adv: Focus on mastering the niche, manual aspects of traditional caulking while familiarizing yourself with digital hull-monitoring sensors and material optimization software.

n.story:
Your role is evolving into that of a precision technician where your manual craftsmanship is guided by digital intelligence. While the physical act of laying fiberglass remains a human-centric skill due to the complexity of custom molds, AI is taking over the tedious preparation and calculation phases. Instead of manually interpreting blueprints and calculating resin ratios, you will use augmented reality and AI to overlay digital templates directly onto your work surface, ensuring perfect alignment and zero material waste.

As AI handles the 'heavy lifting' of technical documentation and chemical process optimization, you become a high-level troubleshooter. When structural anomalies appear or resin cures unexpectedly, you will consult AI-powered technical assistants that can instantly cross-reference thousands of engineering drawings and material science papers to provide a solution. Your value shifts from simple labor to the high-stakes verification of structural integrity and regulatory compliance, using AI to 'see' defects that the human eye might miss.
auto: Basic blueprint interpretation and BOM generation
amp: Rapid cross-referencing of maritime and safety regulations
n.adv: Develop your skills in reading 3D digital models and familiarize yourself with computer-aided quality inspection tools to stay ahead of the shift toward high-tech manufacturing.
